Sulphur_ic_lora_crossview.json.title: New Camera Angle
Sulphur_ic_lora_crossview.json.note:
## How to move the camera

This re-shoots your clip from a new position, like a second camera on the same take, and keeps your clip's sound so it lines up in the edit.

1. Upload **Your source video**. No opening image is needed.
2. Write only the camera move, in these exact words:

`crossview. new camera angle: to the left, higher, closer.`

- **Side:** same angle · slightly to the left · slightly to the right · to the left · to the right · far to the left · far to the right
- **Height:** lower · same height · higher
- **Distance:** closer · same distance · further

3. Run. For a big move, feed the result back in and make another small one.

Small moves are the most reliable. The range is about 60° either side of the front, so a view from behind is out of reach. **IC-LoRA strength** starts at 1.5 because the effect is weaker on fast sampling; 1.2 to 1.5 is the useful range. This is a v0.9 proof of concept, and it was trained on the plain LTX-2.3 model.

**Width** and **Height** set the frame's area, and your clip sets its shape. **Frames** sets the length, and the shot stops at the end of your clip.

Sulphur_ic_lora_ingredients.json.title: Recurring Characters
Sulphur_ic_lora_ingredients.json.note:
## How to keep a character across shots

1. Upload one **Reference sheet** on a black background with no text: a face close-up and a full-body view of each person, each important prop, and a clean panel of the location. Bigger panels carry over better.
2. Keep the prompt's two parts. **Reference sheet:** names each panel by its position. **Generated video:** describes the action and shot.
3. Run. Reuse the same sheet and the same descriptions for every shot of the scene.

The sheet guides the shot and is never seen in the result. It is stretched to the frame, so make it the same shape. 768 x 448, 121 frames at 24 fps is what the model was trained on; other sizes and longer clips drift. Lightricks tuned **IC-LoRA strength** at 1.4 and start their examples at 1.0.

**This one needs a licence first.** Accept the LTX-2 Community License at [Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Ingredients](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Ingredients) with the Hugging Face account behind `HF_TOKEN`, then restart the Pod or run `python3 /opt/sulphur/scripts/download-models.py` in its terminal. Until then this workflow reports a missing LoRA; nothing else is affected.

Sulphur_ic_lora_relight.json.title: Relight
Sulphur_ic_lora_relight.json.note:
## How to relight a shot

1. Upload **Your source video**. This model was made for sunlit exteriors, and it works best on footage with no strong light direction already, such as an overcast day.
2. Set **Light direction**. Rotation 0 lights the scene from the camera's side, 90 from the right, 180 from behind and -90 from the left. The ball is added to the corner of the frame the model reads, and is not in the result.
3. Keep the prompt's first sentence and match its end to the ball:

`relight the video to match the light-direction ball. hard low-angle sunlight from the right`

- **From:** the front · the front-right · the right · the back-right · behind · the back-left · the left · the front-left
- **Looks:** hard directional sunlight · hard high-angle sunlight · hard low-angle sunlight · soft diffused daylight · soft warm afternoon light · cool soft daylight · dim overcast light · strong backlight with rim light · soft hazy backlight · warm golden low front sun · warm golden low side sun · frontal sunlight

Describe the light only, not the scene, and use one light setup per clip. If the words and the ball disagree, the ball wins. The default ball, elevation 15 at intensity 2, follows Lightricks' example. A higher sun brightens the ball's grey background, so lower **intensity** as you raise **elevation**: about 0.8 at elevation 45. Your clip's sound is kept. 1280 x 704, 121 frames at 24 fps is what the model was trained on, and it works in a single pass only.

**Width** and **Height** set the frame's area, and your clip sets its shape. **Frames** sets the length, and the shot stops at the end of your clip.

**This one needs a licence first.** Accept the LTX-2 Community License at [Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Relight](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Relight) with the Hugging Face account behind `HF_TOKEN`, then restart the Pod or run `python3 /opt/sulphur/scripts/download-models.py` in its terminal. Until then this workflow reports a missing LoRA; nothing else is affected.

Sulphur_ic_lora_day_to_night.json.title: Day to Night
Sulphur_ic_lora_day_to_night.json.note:
## How to turn day into night

1. Upload **Your source video**, shot in daylight at 24 fps.
2. Describe the night look and keep the last sentence, which holds the shot still. Steer the colour with phrases such as warm tungsten light or cool white LED light.
3. Run. Composition, camera and motion come from your clip, and its sound is kept.

768 x 448, 97 frames at 24 fps is what the model was trained on; longer clips drift towards the end. On the fast settings here **CFG** stays at 1. Lightricks' own recipe is 30 steps at CFG 3 to 4, where higher is darker.

**Width** and **Height** set the frame's area, and your clip sets its shape. **Frames** sets the length, and the shot stops at the end of your clip.

**This one needs a licence first.** Accept the LTX-2 Community License at [Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Day-To-Night](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Day-To-Night) with the Hugging Face account behind `HF_TOKEN`, then restart the Pod or run `python3 /opt/sulphur/scripts/download-models.py` in its terminal. Until then this workflow reports a missing LoRA; nothing else is affected.
